title: Runtime: log active hardware profile + detected GPU info at startup
author: Omar El-Sayed
description: Why: During profile-pack canaries and Dedicated escalations, on-call often has to answer the same questions quickly: which hardware did the runtime detect (SKU, driver/CUDA, MIG), which profile/version was selected, and which high-impact knobs are actually active. Today that info is spread across multiple logs/config dumps and is easy to miss (and sometimes not included in the standard debug bundle). What: Add a single structured INFO log at runtime startup that summarizes detected hardware + selected profile + a curated set of knob values that materially affect perf/latency and safety. The log is intended to be stable (key names) and machine-readable for ingestion/grep, and safe for customer environments (no secrets; no full config dump). How: - Introduce `runtime.profile_startup_summary` logger that emits one JSON log line after hardware detection + profile selection completes (and after any override guardrails are applied). - Include: `profile_id`, `profile_version`, `selection_reason`, `override_source` (none|fleet_default|customer_pin|env_override), detected GPU `sku`, `gpu_count`, `mig_mode`, `driver_version`, `cuda_runtime_version`, and limited host hints (numa nodes count, cpu model string trimmed). - Include curated knobs only (not the entire profile): scheduler mode + bucket config id, `max_concurrency`, queue limits, batching caps, prefill/decode prioritization, attention kernel variant + fallback policy, KV cache headroom + compaction thresholds, allocator/fragmentation guardrails (high-level). - Add `--log-profile-startup-summary=false` / config flag for Private environments that want to disable this line (default: enabled). - Add unit tests to ensure: (1) summary is emitted once, (2) keys are stable, (3) no high-cardinality per-GPU UUIDs are logged, (4) override_source is correct. Notes: This complements PR-25014 (/health + debug endpoints) but is intentionally available even when endpoints are restricted. Also aligns with INT-8831 (include active profile in on-call debug bundle) by making it reliably present in logs.
commits: runtime/logging: add ProfileStartupSummary struct + JSON formatter
runtime/hw-detect: expose sku/mig/driver/cuda fields to summary builder
runtime/profile: plumb selection_reason + override_source into selection result
tests: add golden snapshot test for startup summary log keys/values
review_conversation: Allison Grant (review): Can we ensure this is exactly one line and stable keys? We should avoid logging per-GPU UUID / PCI bus IDs due to cardinality + customer sensitivity. Also please align field names with the metrics tags we just added (profile_id, sku).

Omar El-Sayed (author): Yep. Updated to emit a single JSON line (no multiline pretty printing) and removed uuid/bus_id. Keys now match `profile_id` and `sku`, and I added a golden snapshot test to lock the key set.

Sean Gallagher (review): Request: make sure we don’t log before guardrails are applied. On-call needs the final effective values. Also, can we include an explicit `override_source` so we can see if a Dedicated customer pin is active during an incident?
Omar El-Sayed (author): Moved emission to after `apply_guardrails()` and included `override_source` + `selection_reason` from selection result. Added unit test for customer pin path.

Noah Patel (review): This is good, but please keep the knob list curated. Don’t include nested objects or full bucket maps; it becomes a config dump. For scheduler buckets, can you log a `bucket_config_id` / hash instead?
Omar El-Sayed (author): Agreed. Replaced bucket map with `scheduler_bucket_config_id` (short hash) and kept only high-impact scalar knobs. No nested maps/arrays in the JSON line.
Connor O'Brien (review): Looks fine for 1.22. Please add a short note to the internal runtime config reference about the new flag and the fact that this log line is part of the expected debug bundle.
Omar El-Sayed (author): Added docs line under logging flags + linked INT-8831 in the note.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved. Snapshot test is exactly what we needed.
Sean Gallagher (approval): Approved. Emission timing after guardrails is correct.
release_notes: On startup, runtime now logs a single structured summary of detected hardware + selected profile/version + key knob values to aid on-call triage (can be disabled via `log_profile_startup_summary=false`).
